A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATLAS research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original calibration, adaptive-evaluation, and model-ranking results on five principal benchmarks, plus experiments on three MMLU subjects in Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 reports original adaptive-evaluation results, comparative model-fit diagnostics, accuracy-reconstruction results, and experiments covering all 57 MMLU subjects.

M1.justification: The core 3PL calibration, common-person linking, WLE references, EAP updates, and top-five randomesque selection remain. V2 adds p-IRT accuracy reconstruction and revises the stated Fisher-information expression in Equation 2. These are localized scoring and mathematical-specification changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding code changes.

E1.justification: The five principal benchmarks remain. MMLU coverage expands from Anatomy, Astronomy, and High School Macroeconomics in v1 Appendix G to all 57 subjects in v2 Appendix G.3, adding substantial coverage of domains such as law, computer science, and philosophy.

E2.justification: The four main performance baselines remain Random, TinyBenchmarks, MetaBench-Primary, and MetaBench-Secondary. However, v1 Appendix D reports only ATLAS model fit, whereas v2 Table 1 adds TinyBenchmarks and MetaBench as evaluated comparators in that diagnostic comparison. Fluid Benchmarking is discussed but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: V2 introduces accuracy-reconstruction evaluation and the Information Efficiency Score alongside ability MAE. Reported baseline settings also change: GSM8K MetaBench-Primary/Secondary use 237/249 items in v2 Table 6 instead of 100/100 in v1 Table 1. Filtered bank sizes change, including HellaSwag from 5,608 to 5,600 items.

E4.justification: V2 adds comparative calibration-fit diagnostics and an explicit check of whether estimated abilities recover full-benchmark accuracy. It removes v1 Section 4.5's negative-discrimination analysis, WinoGrande item #247 example, and quantified information-weighting argument. Existing rank comparisons and heatmap case studies are largely retained; the additional MMLU subjects extend coverage rather than introduce a new ablation.

E5.justification: V2 adds MAE standard errors, calculated from absolute-error variation across models, to the principal performance tables. These are not repeated-run uncertainties. Conversely, v1 Table 4's averaged 5th/95th-percentile RMSEA bounds disappear. Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Results are substantially revised. From v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 2, HellaSwag ATLAS0.1 changes from 0.154 MAE with 39 items to 0.157 with 41; MetaBench-P/S MAEs change from 0.164/0.238 to 0.514/1.570. Changed reported conditions prevent interpreting these as clean version-to-version performance gains. V2 also adds reconstruction, IES, comparator-fit, and 54 additional MMLU subjects' results, updates exposure/overlap values, and removes the 3.2–5.7% negative-discrimination finding.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes from a_i^2 p_i(1-p_i) to (p_i')^2/[p_i(1-p_i)], a nonequivalent correction for the stated 3PL model. V2 also introduces the IES definition and p-IRT conditional-expectation/MMSE formulation in Appendices E–F, and removes v1's assertion that EAP is undefined for extreme response patterns. No substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: V2 removes contamination resistance and detection of annotation errors from the headline contributions, qualifies item reduction as 'up to 90%', and drops the 'first large-scale' novelty claim. It instead foregrounds accuracy reconstruction, precision-controlled evaluation, model-fit validation, and linking. The central efficiency and ability-discrimination claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 emphasizes calibration misfit, scale alignment, and preservation of global accuracy, while retreating from v1's strong contamination-protection interpretation. V1 Section 5.2's substantive limitations concerning calibration drift, multiple-choice applicability, and unidimensional ability modeling are removed rather than relocated. Appendix discussion still associates low exposure with reduced contamination risk.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents a ten-bin stratified 90/10 calibration/test split and separate testing counts in Section 3.2 and Table 5; this alone does not establish that v1 lacked a holdout. V1's explicit mirt/R implementation note and parameter-exclusion thresholds are omitted. The code and calibrated-bank access claim remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions ATLAS relative to newly discussed Fluid Benchmarking, distinguishing post-training evaluation and precision-based stopping from Fluid's described focus. It withdraws the 'first large-scale' claim, expands criticism of static methods through fit diagnostics, and adds benchmark, CAT, and benchmark-quality references. These changes exceed citation-format or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, results narrative, discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Appendices are reordered and consolidated, the existing linking procedure receives an expanded explanation, and an Impact Statement is added while the explicit limitations section disappears. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond added experimental content.

P2.justification: Performance tables gain SE and IES columns and are split between main-text and appendix benchmark groups; separate reconstruction tables and a comparative fit table are introduced. The MMLU table becomes a multipage display. Figures are redrawn with revised typography, grids, labels, and captions, and Figures 4–6 are consolidated onto one page.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical consistency through the corrected information formula and removal of the conflicting EAP assertion, while narrowing overstated headline claims. Accuracy-reconstruction checks, performance standard errors, and broader MMLU coverage strengthen validation. These gains support a positive but limited net assessment because v2 also removes important applicability limitations and some reproducibility disclosures.
